description: Rapid linear peeled transfers along a single chain: funds hop through a short chain of fresh intermediate wallets before reaching the final target.
Swap volatile assets into a stablecoin on the origin chain, then bridge the proceeds to a target chain before final transfer to the destination wallet.
One-to-N splitting: the source fans funds out into multiple parallel intermediate nodes on the same chain, which later converge into an aggregator before the final target.
Layered chain hopping across three distinct chains: funds bridge from chain A to chain B, then immediately bridge again to chain C, where they are finally transferred to the target.
N-to-1 integration: several source streams merge into a single aggregator node, which then transfers the consolidated funds to the final target.
Asset conversion through a decentralized exchange liquidity pool: funds are transferred into a swap node and converted into a different asset before reaching the target.
Deep layered peeling chain: a long sequence of linear hops through intermediate wallets on one chain, maximising the number of hops before reaching the target.
Round-trip bridging: funds leave the origin chain through a bridge, pass through an intermediate chain, and are bridged back to the origin chain before final settlement.
Mixer-style anonymisation: funds are swapped through an asset-conversion node, split into parallel streams, and merged back into an aggregator before the final target.
Repeated same-chain asset conversions: funds are swapped through multiple conversion nodes in sequence to obfuscate the asset trail before the final transfer.
Cross-chain layered integration: two source streams merge on the origin chain and are bridged to the target chain, where they merge again with a local stream before settlement.
Split-then-bridge fan-out: funds are split into parallel streams on the origin chain and each stream is bridged to a different destination chain before re-converging on the final target chain.

Iterative peeling chain: a source or continuation node splits value asymmetrically into a dominant continuation edge and a minor peel edge; the continuation repeats the split and minor peel edges terminate at targets.

Source distributes incoming funds via multiple split edges to a first layer of intermediate nodes, each of which further splits funds to additional intermediate nodes, forming a layered fan-out distribution structure.
Funds from multiple sources merge into a mixer aggregator, then are split into fragmented withdrawals to targets, breaking the link between deposit and withdrawal.
Cross-chain bridge hop to a less-monitored chain, optionally preceded by asset conversion, followed by transfer through a reconstructed destination address.
Multiple victim source accounts merge chaotic irregular inflows into one or few attacker core aggregation wallets, forming consolidation peaks; source accounts are victims and not part of the gang.

Illicit crypto flows fragmented across source branches converge into the attacker's source-chain consolidation wallet, are bridged to a target chain, then transferred into the target-chain OTC/P2P acceptor deposit address for off-chain cash-out.

Stolen asset streams on several chains are converted and bridged into a primary-chain aggregator, then split through downstream mule layers to same-chain OTC acceptors and cross-chain exit branches, ending in target-chain cash-out addresses.
Illicitly minted assets are consolidated on the origin chain, bridged to the target chain, then split into a returned portion and an attacker-controlled self-transfer stream.

Unauthorized asset creation on the source chain is spent through intermediate relay addresses, split across two bridge paths to the target chain, and delivered to two target-chain cash-out destinations.
Cross-chain bridge abuse leads to asset conversion and a final transfer into a mixing sink on the destination chain.

Borrowed value is swapped through a manipulated liquidity venue into an illiquid asset, with the underlying value captured by two attacker-controlled positions; those positions bridge to a second abstract chain, consolidate into a destination wallet, and then split between a privacy sink and a residual wallet.

Drained assets are converted into a native asset, split across multiple mule addresses, then portions are consolidated into a mixer aggregator and another portion swapped into a stable asset held at a final wallet.
Exploit-origin funds bridge from the origin chain to a target chain, pass through an intermediate relay, undergo an asset conversion, then are split across four target wallets for dispersal.

End-to-end exploit proceeds are converted on the origin chain, routed through an intermediate layer, bridged to the destination chain, converted again through a swap, and transferred into a shielded target sink.
Source obtains flash-loan capital, swaps into a manipulated token, sells into the pool to extract stablecoin, then splits proceeds to an exchange cash-out address and a mixer sink.

A source exploits a contract to mint token without cost, swaps token into native_asset, then splits proceeds across attacker-controlled intermediates; one branch is dispersed to holding targets and a secondary branch is transferred to a mixer target.
Repeated batch swaps inflate an internal accounting balance; withdrawn proceeds are then split into batched relay transfers before consolidation into a mixer target.

Abstract full-loop campaign: initial mixer funding to attacker/helper, pool manipulation and liquidity extraction via swap, consolidation of proceeds, then split into major and minor batch series sent to mixer deposit targets.

Unified campaign: an exchange source funds a deployer that seeds a liquidity pool; a prior reserve source splits funds through an infrastructure contract to mule addresses that swap into the pool to fabricate volume; the pool is drained to an attacker-controlled intermediate, sold through an asset-conversion venue, and the proceeds consolidate into a fund-holding aggregator before splitting between cash-out and future campaign funding.
Cross-chain peg-out of an unbacked origin-chain asset to a destination chain, followed by a split of proceeds between a returned portion and a retained portion.
Cross-chain deposit triggers a minted synthetic representation on an intermediate chain, followed by a DEX swap into another asset and a bridge to a final destination chain.
